prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a narrow interior layout with walls and door panels close to the wearer (about 0.3–1 m), a floor extending forward, and an open doorway leading to a brighter, more distant area (roughly 2–4 m); brighter regions clarify which door edges and wall surfaces project nearest even where RGB texture is confusing. Across frames 1–3, the wearer turns and advances slightly around the doorway, so nearby door and wall planes sweep laterally while the central floor remains farther away; in frames 4–5 the view rotates right toward a person about 1–2 m ahead and slightly right. The person in frame 5 is nearer than much of the background but is partly cut off by the top and right borders, and the map does not reliably separate the person's limbs from adjacent structures. Absolute metre estimates are uncertain because this is monocular depth, and several bright doorway regions appear saturated or influenced by lighting rather than true proximity.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates people and a small cell phone, making partial foreground bodies and hands near the bottom edge easier to distinguish from the floor and doors; most such fragments are within roughly 0.2–0.8 m of the camera and are likely parts of the wearer or people extremely close to the viewpoint. Across frames 1–3, person masks remain largely clipped along the lower edge while a small phone-sized object appears left of centre in frame 2, about 1–2 m away in the RGB context; frames 4–5 add several overlapping person masks, including a standing person ahead-right at roughly 1–2 m. The masks reveal strong occlusion and truncation—bodies overlap one another or leave the frame—and show relative left/right placement, but they provide little direct distance or facing information. Reliability is poor in places: large door or wall regions are labelled “umbrella,” the far-right object is labelled “skateboard,” and fragmented person masks make counts and separations between people uncertain.
descriptions.pose: The pose map exposes articulated locations that are difficult to pick out in the RGB: a magenta hand near the lower-left area of frame 1, several hands around the centre and right of frame 4, and a yellow body skeleton for the standing person at the far right of frame 5. The frame-5 skeleton places that person about 1–2 m ahead-right, upright and angled roughly sideways toward the left side of the scene rather than clearly facing the camera; the head and part of the body are near or beyond the upper-right border. Frame 4 shows nearby hands and partial arm/body joints within approximately 0.3–1.5 m, including one extended structure running rightward, but missing torso connections prevent reliable assignment to particular people or determination of who is in front of whom. Sparse or absent detections in frames 2–3, floating joints, clipped limbs, and implausible connections make reach, gaze direction, and changes in approach or retreat much less reliable than coarse orientation and limb position.
